So this      adapter is PULL-driven \u2014 a relayer calls `receiveAndExecute(payload, signature)`, the adapter calls      `gatewayMint` itself, then acts on the payload it parsed from the same attested bytes.PERMISSIONLESS: anyone can call `receiveAndExecute`. Safety is anchored by:      1. Circle's attestation signature covering the entire payload (incl. `account` and `hookData`); every         attestation is value-backed by a Circle-verified deposit, so there is no forged-message primitive.      2. `destinationCaller = adapter` (enforced by the minter when non-zero) keeping mint + execution atomic.      3. A      revert BEFORE the mint therefore costs the user a retry, not funds \u2014 so every content problem (routing,      token, undecodable hookData, bad account, mixed set) is rejected pre-mint. checkDestinationTargets(bytes).details: External ONLY so the entrypoints can self-call it and contain `abi.decode` panics on a malformed      `sigData`. Returns a code rather than reverting so the caller can distinguish "malformed blob"      (caught, treated as MATCH_OK) from "explicit mismatch" (funds delivered, execution skipped).      MUST only be called by this contract.

params.sigData: The raw SignatureData blob from the hookData

returns.code: MATCH_OK when the proof matches or no proof exists for this chain

params.gatewayMinter_: Circle Gateway minter on this chain
params.usdc_: USDC token on this chain (must be minter-supported)

decodeHookPayload(bytes).details: External ONLY so the entrypoints can self-call it and contain `abi.decode` panics on a malformed tail.      MUST only be called by this contract.

receiveAndExecute(bytes,bytes).details: PERMISSIONLESS — see contract-level NatSpec. Every content check runs BEFORE `gatewayMint`; a revert      there leaves the TransferSpec hash unused, the attestation expires and the balance is restored.A homogeneous AttestationSet (identical caller/recipient/token/hookData across members) is minted in      one `gatewayMint`, delivered once and executed once. Mixed sets are rejected.

params.attestationPayload: The raw Attestation or AttestationSet bytes exactly as Circle attested them

recoverDirectMint(bytes).details: PERMISSIONLESS and signature-free. The minter's own `isTransferSpecHashUsed(keccak256(spec))` is a      strictly stronger witness than a signature check: the hash is written only inside `gatewayMint`,      after Circle's signature was verified, and it binds recipient, token, value, `hookData` (so the      `account`) and salt byte-for-byte. Re-verifying the signer here would add nothing and would strand      the funds forever once Circle rotates its attestation signer (review R1-F2). Every member must be used      by the minter and not yet attributed here; only the non-escrowed balance is ever forwarded, never      partially. A payload reconstructed from the public direct-mint calldata is sufficient.

params.attestationPayload: An Attestation or AttestationSet whose member specs were minted (the outer        `maxBlockHeight` is irrelevant here; only the specs are read)

GATEWAY_MINTER().notice: The Circle Gateway minter on this chain (UUPS proxy, same address on every chain)

SUPER_DESTINATION_EXECUTOR().notice: The SuperDestinationExecutor for processing bridged executions

SUPER_DESTINATION_VALIDATOR().notice: The destination validator wired into the executor, cached at construction

USDC().notice: The USDC token Gateway mints on this chain (the only token this adapter delivers)

checkDestinationTargets(bytes).notice: Report whether the DstProof for this chain targets this deployment's executor/validator.

claimFailedTransfer(address,uint256).notice: Claim a previously escrowed balance. Only the recipient can claim its own.

failedTransfers(address,address).notice: Claimable escrow balances (failed delivery or over-mint surplus): account => token => amount

processed(bytes32).notice: TransferSpec hashes this adapter has already attributed (relayed or recovered)

receiveAndExecute(bytes,bytes).notice: Mints the attested USDC through Circle Gateway, forwards it to the intent account and best-effort         executes the signed destination intent.

recoverDirectMint(bytes).notice: Attributes USDC that a spec NOT pinned to this adapter (zero or third-party `destinationCaller`)         minted straight into this adapter without going through `receiveAndExecute` (someone called         `gatewayMint` directly), forwarding it and executing the intent exactly as the relay would have.
